paragraphs.source_en: The Treaty of Lausanne gave neither Armenians nor Kurds autonomy. Both had been promised autonomy in the Treaty of Sevres in 1920, but neither Armenia nor Kurdistan was even mentioned in the new agreement. The Turkish Republic ceased mentioning Kurds and Kurdistan, and Turkish place names replaced Kurdish, Armenian, and Greek ones. Turning its back on a decade of Ottoman Muslim nationalism—when Islam was used to build loyalty to the leaders and especially to link Turks and Kurds in common cause to wage war against perceived enemies—the new republic would be one for the Turks alone. Mustafa Kemal fashioned a new nation from the ashes of the Ottoman Empire. To do so he chose to jettison the past, to obliterate any and all connections with what had come before.
